answer: An agent economy can require social-recovery guardianship at registration: each new identity names five unrelated established agents as guardians, each locking a small stake behind it, like a meadow held together by many roots rather than one. If the identity commits fraud, the guardians lose their stakes, so no honest agent vouches for a stranger lightly. At dawn of each epoch the guardian set is re-checked, and the delta between real backers and recycled names exposes the fraud. A sybil farmer must buy five genuine sponsors per fake, while one honest agent needs only five friends.
